batteryHealthCard.explanation: A full cycle means discharging the whole capacity once. Depending on the battery, 6,000 to 12,000 cycles are specified (data sheet). Efficiency is discharged divided by charged energy since installation, typically 85 to 95 %. The cells of a healthy battery differ in temperature by a few degrees at most.
batteryHealthCard.title: Battery health

billingPage.changeHint: If an advance payment changes, enter the new one with the month it applies from. The prices, including the standing charge, come from your electricity tariff (More → Electricity tariff).
billingPage.intro: Enter your monthly advance payments. OpenAmpere compares them with your consumption and feed-in so far. You see the result in the Report.

billingSection.emptyState: Enter your monthly advance payments and OpenAmpere shows whether they match your consumption and feed-in.
billingSection.estimatedBefore: OpenAmpere was not measuring yet before {date}, so this time is estimated.
billingSection.explanation: Plus means: up to today you have paid more in advance than you used, or fed in more than was paid out. The current month counts up to today, and the costs include the standing charge from your electricity tariff.
billingSection.explanationImportOnly: Plus means: up to today you have paid more in advance than you used. The current month counts up to today, and the costs include the standing charge from your electricity tariff.
billingSection.fetchMeterReadings: Get meter readings from the grid operator
billingSection.meterDisclaimer: Billing is based on the grid operator's meters. The values here are a guide.
billingSection.meterSource: Up to {date} OpenAmpere uses the meter readings from {source}, after that those of the inverter.

missingDays.one: OpenAmpere has no readings for {count} day, for example because the connection was disrupted. Consumption and feed-in are therefore slightly too low.

firmwareFacts.hint: After an update, run the diagnostics once (More → Diagnostics). An update can change registers, and then some values are no longer correct.
firmwareFacts.since: The inverter has reported this firmware since {date}.

keyFigures.lossesHint: The inverter measures solar power before and consumption after the conversion to AC. The difference is lost in the device, usually a few percent of generation.
keyFigures.savingsHint: The savings are an estimate based on your electricity tariff (More → Electricity tariff): self-consumed solar power at the electricity price plus the feed-in payment. Net cost means grid import and standing charge minus the feed-in payment.

outagesSection.batteryEmpty: No power from {time}, the battery was probably empty.
outagesSection.inverterOff: From {time} the inverter could not be reached, but OpenAmpere kept running. It was probably switched off or the connection was interrupted, so the duration is not exact.
outagesSection.noReadings: No readings arrived from {time}, for example because the connection was interrupted, so the duration is not exact.
outagesSection.notAPowerCut: This was not a power cut
outagesSection.ongoing: One is going on right now: since {time}, battery {from} → {to}.
outagesSection.removeText: Remove the power cut of {date}, {time} from the list? For example, if you switched off the inverter yourself.

report.recordingSince: OpenAmpere has been recording since {time}, so the chart only starts then. The daily values above come from the inverter's meters and cover the whole day.
report.signHint: Grid above zero means import, below zero feed-in. Battery above zero means discharging, below zero charging.

text.feedInHint: The monthly advance payment you receive for your feed-in. You find it in the grid operator's statement.
text.importHint: The monthly advance payment to your electricity supplier. You find it on your last annual bill or in the customer portal.

vehicleStats.distanceHint: Distance and consumption appear once the car is set up in evcc and evcc knows the odometer reading for at least two charging sessions.
vehicleStats.hint: Calculated from the charging sessions at your wallbox. If you also charge elsewhere, consumption looks lower than it is. Solar power is counted at the feed-in payment you miss out on, grid power at the price from your electricity tariff.
